problem: Open-vocabulary mobile manipulation systems rely on pre-built maps, static-scene assumptions, or drift-free camera poses. Voxel memories such as DynaMem do not re-align historical semantic observations after SLAM loop closure, and their memory and update time grow without bound over long horizons.
motivation: Service robots in unseen homes and labs face relocated objects, occlusions and continuously refined SLAM pose graphs. Stale or misaligned scene memory then causes wrong navigation targets and failed manipulation. A useful memory must stay geometrically consistent, be semantically queryable, and remain bounded in size and compute.
key_idea: Build an online voxel spatio-semantic memory on a LiDAR-inertial-visual SLAM backend, with pose-graph-aware reintegration and keyframe-guided pruning (RMP), and ground targets via a hybrid pipeline of memory retrieval, open-vocabulary detection and mLLM verification.
insight: Reintegrating observations under optimized poses and pruning non-keyframe history keeps memory nearly flat (0.37-0.63 GB vs DynaMem up to 10.43 GB) and update time at about 0.5 s. The localization ablation shows mLLM verification lifts query success from 77% to 83% by rejecting similar distractors. The grasping ablation shows each component adds gains: heuristic only 67%, AnyGrasp only 79%, AnyGrasp+heuristic 88%, plus two-stage 94%. Note that there is no ablation of RMP's effect on task success.
method: Multi-sensor SLAM backend: Fast-LIO2 (MID-360 LiDAR+IMU) odometry feeds RTAB-Map with D435i RGB-D for loop closure and pose-graph optimization, giving keyframes and optimized poses.

Dynamic voxel memory: sparse voxels store position, count, source image ID, SigLIP feature (weighted average) and last-seen time; new RGB-D points are added, and obsolete voxels are removed by ray casting within 3 m depth.

Redundancy-Aware Memory Pruning: keyframes whose pose changed by >0.1 m or >5° are marked inconsistent. Depending on the fraction inconsistent, the system does Loop-Aware Global Reintegration (>2/3), Regional Reintegration (>1/3 in the 50-frame window plus one in the 10-frame real-time window), Local Refresh, or ignores the update. History is capped at 500 frames and 100 keyframes, and features are kept only for keyframes and the latest 10 frames.

Hybrid localization: the language embedding retrieves the top voxel and its latest RGB image; OWL-v2 detects the object and back-projects it to 3D; Qwen-VL-Max verifies each candidate (True/False). If none survives, the system reports 'object not found' and explores.

Task-oriented navigation: A* on a 2D obstacle map from memory; frontier exploration scored by a recency map plus a semantic-similarity map with a >=0.85 m goal-distance heuristic; a docking point within 0.85 m of the target; receding-horizon execution of 16 waypoints; cached goal replanned if a new detection differs by >0.5 m.

Grasping and placement: Grounding DINO + SAM2 segmentation, AnyGrasp proposals filtered by mask, a PCA top-down heuristic fallback, and two-stage approach (pre-grasp 0.25 m back). Object goes to a rear basket, then is re-grasped and placed into the container at a height of max z + 0.1 m.

setting.backbone: SigLIP-so400m (frozen), OWL-v2 Large ensemble (frozen), Qwen-VL-Max mLLM verifier (frozen), Grounding DINO + SAM2, AnyGrasp (pretrained)
setting.observation: Wrist-mounted RGB-D (RealSense D435i) plus 3D LiDAR + IMU (Livox MID-360), SLAM poses
setting.action_space: A* waypoints on a 2D grid to docking pose for a holonomic base (AgileX Ranger Mini 3.0), plus xArm6 grasp/place end-effector trajectories
setting.privileged: none (target is manually relocated by a human during runs; no pre-built map)

numbers_note: No standard navigation benchmark; real-robot results in four lab scenes (S1-S4) only, not in the canonical benchmark list, so no entries are given. Key results: long-term success 70/65/60/55% (S1-S4) vs DynaMem 60/55/40/40%; aggregate 50/80=62.5% vs 39/80=48.8%; navigation success 89.2/86.1/83.8/80.0%; memory 0.37/0.46/0.61/0.63 GB; update time 0.43/0.49/0.53/0.52 s.
results: On a real robot in four dynamic lab scenes, DREAM reaches 55-70% long-term success versus 40-60% for DynaMem (aggregate 62.5% vs 48.8%), with larger navigation gains in cluttered S3/S4 (83.8/80.0 vs 72.7/68.8). Memory is 0.37-0.63 GB versus DynaMem's 1.32-10.43 GB, and update time is 0.43-0.53 s versus DynaMem's 0.82-2.38 s and DovSG's more than 110 s.
limitations: Small real-world sample (20 long-horizon trials per scene; the Wilson 95% CIs of the aggregates overlap), only one baseline (DynaMem) in closed loop, and no ablation isolating RMP's effect on task success.
Modular heuristic pipeline accumulates errors over long horizons, and manipulation is limited to pick-and-place (no contact-rich or articulated objects).
Depends on a heavy LiDAR-visual SLAM stack, a remote GPU server and a cloud mLLM; evaluated only in single-room lab scenes, with target relocation done manually.
